sentences.text:
THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 26.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2 MACA 4185/2019 Fasaludeen.P.M vs Maharajan.P on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168762638/
1  2025:KER:73375  JUDGMENT
(Dated this the 26th day of September 2025)

The appellant, who was the petitioner in OP(MV)
No.1353 of 2016
before the Additional MACT, Pathanamthitta, has come up with this appeal for enhancement of compensation awarded to him by the Tribunal.
The Petition was filed under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

2. On 5.9.2016, while the appellant was standing on the side of the Pathanapuram- Punalur public road near Kadakkamn Thaikkavu junction, one lorry bearing reg. No.TN-69-AB-8641 driven by the 1st respondent from west to east, in a rash and negligent manner, hit the appellant and caused severe injuries to him.
He was taken to St.Joseph hospital, Pathanapuram and from there, he was referred to N. S. Memorial hospital, Kollam, where he was treated as inpatient till 9.9.2016.

Hence,
the OP was filed claiming a compensation of 15,00,250/- limited to 5,00,250/-.
2. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the owner and insurer of the vehicle.
Before the Tribunal, respondent Nos.1 and 2 remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent filed a written 2025:KER:73375 statement admitting the policy and contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, he claimed that the accident happened not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle and the claim by the appellant was also stated to be exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of O.P.
3.

The Tribunal, on an elaborate consideration of the Exhibits produced as Ext.A1 to A15, found that the accident was due to the negligence of the 1st respondent and awarded a total compensation of 6,51,418/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from 6.10.2016 till realisation.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads, this appeal is filed.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the standing counsel for 3rd respondent.
5. The counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal went wrong in taking the monthly income as 8,000/- for calculating compensation for permanent disability.

Going by the decision reported in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 2025:KER:73375 Insurance Co.
Ltd [(2011) 13 SCC 236], even for a coolie who met with an accident in the year 2016, the notional monthly income fixed is 10,500/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I fix the same as the monthly income for the purpose of calculating the permanent disability compensation.
Ext.A12 is the disability certificate issued by the Taluk head quarters hospital, Ranni, which shows that the appellant sustained 16% permanent disability.
Since the appellant is aged 50 years at the time of accident, the multiplier to be adopted is 13, which is correctly adopted by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the compensation towards permanent disability can be recalculated as 10,500x13x12x16/100 = 2,62,080/-.
6. The compensation claimed under the loss of earning was granted for 6 months.
The appellant sustained comminuted compound fracture left humerous, lacerated wound over left shoulder, left Fasaludeen.

2 arm.
etc, and he was treated as inpatient for 11 days in 2 spells in 3 different hospitals.
On going through Ext.A10 and A11, I am of the view that the period considered by the Tribunal for loss of earning as 6 months is less.

Therefore, considering the gravity of the 2025:KER:73375 injuries sustained and treatments followed for over a long period of time, I am inclined to grant compensation under the loss of earning for 12 months.
Thus, the compensation under the said head can be re

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and injuries sustained by the appellant, the compensation for pain and sufferings awarded by the Tribunal also can be enhanced by 1,00,000/-
more.
8. On a perusal of the order of the Tribunal, I am satisfied that just and reasonable compensation has been granted under all other heads.

9. Accordingly, the following enhancements are made to the award passed by the Tribunal:
Sl. Head of Claim Amt. Awarded by Amt. Enhanced No. Tribunal (Rs.) in appeal (Rs.)
1 Compensation for permanent 1,99,680 2,62,080 disability 2. Loss of earning 48,000 1,26,000 3 Pain and suffering 1,00,000 2,00,000

In the result, this appeal is allowed and the appellant is entitled for an enhanced amount of 2,40,400/- (Rupees two lakh forty thousand and four hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. over and above the amount awarded by the Tribunal from the date of petition till realisation.
All other findings entered by the Tribunal stand confirmed.
If any amounts have already been paid, the same shall be granted set off.

The claimant shall produce the details of the Bank account before the Insurance Company/Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and amount shall be transferred to the Bank account directly through NEFT/RTGS mode, within a period of one month thereafter.
If the Bank account is not furnished within the time stipulated, it is made clear that no interest shall run on the enhanced amount after the period stipulated by this Court.

SD/-
BASANT BALAJI JUDGE dl/
